newsitem.title: USA: Washington state Gov. signs business tax rollback.
newsitem.headline: Washington state Gov. signs business tax rollback.

text.p: Washington state Gov. Gary Locke signed legislation to roll back business and occupation tax rates to 1.5 percent for nearly 70,000 service businesses, his office said Tuesday.

The rollback, which will take effect in July 1998, will reduce state general fund revenues by an estimated $94.3 million in the fiscal year beginning July 1, 1998 and by about $114.7 million in the fiscal year beginning July 1, 1999, the state's department of revenue said.

The business and occupation tax measure signed by Locke, a Democrat, will reduce the tax rate to the pre-1993 level of 1.5 percent. The tax rate was raised in 1993 to deal with the state's budget shortfall.
The rollback will benefit nearly 70,000 service businesses in Washington state, including accountants, lawyers and engineers.
In March, Locke vetoed a similar tax measure because it would have taken effect this July, forcing immediate cuts in education and human services funding.
